cases.name: owner_rounds_and_one_line_per_run
cases.description: The owner's request heads the start round; each later instruction of theirs heads a round of its own. A run's turns in a round are one line, its latest summary with how many turns; the run works now, so its line in the latest round is live and says what it does. Persona's relays fold under the round they fall in, with the run they reached when the relay names it. A run is named by its session's title (the session list's, renamed since the link), and the hand-off card that started it says nothing its link does not.

cases.name: background_round_per_day_in_the_owners_zone
cases.description: Supervision nobody asked for (a rework, the run's report to its supervisor, a park, the overdue mark, a review waiting to be done) forms one Background round per day in the owner's zone (Tokyo here): 14:50 and 15:10 UTC are one UTC day but two Tokyo days. Each Background round sits among the owner's rounds by its first entry's time. The paper shows the latest two rounds that are not Background ones: the start round and the owner's round, which holds the ask, though both Background rounds began after it. A needs_user review the background supervisor gave stays in its round, since it asks the owner.
source: docs/design/proposals/todos-redesign.md 3.6 ("one folded Background round per day")

cases.name: failed_starts
cases.description: Each failed start is one line. A run whose own start failed is the same failure as the receipt written with it, which then names the run and its error; such a run never starts or ends. The latest failure, which the to-do's start error belongs to, says that error as a line. Where the hub kept an error, the line says it and the receipt's words are left out; a failure nothing names an error for keeps the receipt's words, the hub's sentence as the conversation showed it.

cases.name: results_close_and_recap
cases.description: What the work produced: the code change a receipt named (at that receipt, with how the hub last saw it; the receipt wrote its address in other letters, and one PR is one chip), the work going live, and what it came to (the hub's outcome line, with the first link it named); an earlier change the hub only looked at is the fourth result and is left out. The outcome's decisions and pitfalls are the run's decisions. The done judge accepted the work and closed the to-do (the hub's, both). Since the owner looked, everything counts in the recap but their own answer and the hub's relay of it, which folds under it; the recap points at the round of the first change.
